paragraphs.source_en: 2. “As the History of Warfare Makes Clear, Potential for Catastrophe Remains,” Los Angeles Times, February 23, 1991, 20. 3. During Desert Storm, the United States destroyed bunkers of Iraqi chemical weapons at Tallil. By 1998, UNSCOM had eliminated or overseen the destruction of more than eighty thousand chemical munitions and tons of bulk chemical agents. 4. A great deal of controversy erupted over whether the war was ended too early in that two Republican Guard divisions escaped to Basra. This debate generally ignored the fact that Iraq had maintained more than twenty army divisions (770,000 soldiers) in Iraq, safely positioned far from the theater of operations.
